basic_identification.name: fxhash $FXH token and bonding curves
basic_identification.originator: fxhash team (ciphrd/Johann Music, founder); backed by 1kx (lead), Fabric Ventures, Union Square Ventures, Coinbase Ventures; $5M seed (August 2023)
basic_identification.geography: France (founding); global platform; originally Tezos, now multichain (Ethereum, Base L2)

core_ideas.core_claim: A decentralized generative art ecosystem that introduces art coins via bonding curves on Base L2, enabling artists to create ERC-20 tokens linked to their collections. This creates multiple revenue streams beyond one-time sales and royalties — artists earn 75% of ongoing trading fees on their art coin's liquidity pool. The system introduces 'open-form' generative art where collectors spend art coins to mint, evolve, burn, or lock editions.
core_ideas.medium_specificity: Deeply medium-specific. Generative art (code-based, hash-determined) is the core practice. The art coin mechanism is native to programmable money — bonding curves, liquidity pools, and token-gated minting are only possible on blockchain. Open-form art (collector-driven minting using art coins) creates a new category where the economic layer and the creative layer are structurally integrated. fx(params) allows collectors to write code that shapes outputs, up to 512 characters.
core_ideas.relation_to_attention_economy: Complex dual relationship. The art coin and bonding curve mechanics introduce speculative attention dynamics — token prices respond to hype cycles, and 'graduation' of bonding curves incentivizes early speculation. However, the underlying generative art practice resists attention economy by requiring code literacy, long-form exploration, and aesthetic judgment. The fx(params) co-creation model demands sustained attention (deep engagement with parameter spaces) rather than fleeting clicks. The tension between speculation-driven token attention and practice-driven creative attention is the platform's central dynamic.
core_ideas.relation_to_intention: Mixed. The generative art marketplace infrastructure serves declared structural needs (artist compensation, collector engagement, on-chain art). The art coin mechanism introduces attention-capture dynamics through speculation. The 75/25 fee split and continuous revenue model serve artist intention. But bonding curve graduation mechanics can prioritize financial speculation over artistic merit.

market_economics.revenue_model: Multiple layers: (1) Platform fees on primary NFT mints. (2) Art coins via bonding curves — 1% trading fee on primary liquidity pool split 75% artist / 25% fxhash. (3) $FXH token (1B total supply; 40% community airdrop, 30% team/investors with 1-year cliff/3-year vest). (4) Collectors spend art coins + ETH fee to mint open-form editions. (5) Minting/evolving escrows art coins, burning releases them, locking permanently removes supply.
market_economics.market_position: Primary market (generative art minting) and secondary market (art coin trading, NFT trading). Infrastructure for artist-collector economic relationships. Competes with Art Blocks (curated generative art) and Prohibition (on Arbitrum).
market_economics.price_range: Wide range. Generative art editions from 0.001 ETH to several ETH. Art coins launched at bonding curve start prices (fractions of cents). $FXH trading at ~$0.0009 (down 97% from ATH of $0.035). Blue-chip fxhash works (early Tezos era) trade at significant premiums on secondary.
market_economics.volume_trend_2024_2026: Growing through pivot. Migrated from Tezos-only to multichain (Ethereum, Base). Art coin launches began July 2025 (launch artists: $CIPHRD, $P1XEL, $EBOY, $SLIPS). $FXH token listed on Coinbase. Market cap ~$491K — very small. Volume trend upward from low base but token price has declined significantly from launch.
market_economics.collector_demographics: Crypto-native generative art collectors. Code-literate audience that values algorithmic aesthetics. Significant overlap with Art Blocks community. Early Tezos community was notably less speculative and more practice-oriented than Ethereum NFT collectors. The Base migration and art coins may shift demographics toward more speculative participants.
market_economics.sustainability: The art coin model creates continuous revenue streams (trading fees) rather than one-time sales, which is structurally more sustainable. However, sustainability depends on trading volume, which depends on speculative interest. If speculation fades, trading fees collapse. The generative art practice itself has proven durable through the crash, but the token layer's sustainability is unproven. VC funding ($5M seed) provides runway but creates growth expectations.

practice_aesthetics.toolchain: JavaScript/p5.js/Three.js/GLSL/WebGL for generative art creation. Solidity smart contracts for bonding curves and art coins. Base L2 (Ethereum) and Tezos blockchains. IPFS for metadata storage. On-chain hash for deterministic output generation. fx(params) system for parametric collector input (up to 512 characters of code/parameters).
practice_aesthetics.relation_to_AI: Neutral to cautious. fxhash is primarily a code-art platform — generative art written by human artists in JavaScript/GLSL. AI is not a core tool or medium. Some artists may use AI in their creative process, but the platform's identity is rooted in hand-coded generative systems. The emphasis on code authorship, hash-determinism, and on-chain reproducibility implicitly values human programming over AI generation.
practice_aesthetics.liveness: Generative — each mint produces a unique output from the same code via hash. Open-form works are evolving (collectors can mint new editions, evolve existing ones). Art coins create a live economic layer. The artwork itself is static once minted but the collection is living/growing through open-form mechanics.
practice_aesthetics.aesthetic_vocabulary: Rich and established within generative art: hash-determinism, parametric space, long-form vs. curated, edition size, entropy, signed distance functions, rayhatcher, procedural generation. The art coin mechanism introduces new vocabulary: bonding curve graduation, art coin escrow, open-form minting. fxhash has been central to developing the critical vocabulary of on-chain generative art since 2021.
practice_aesthetics.tendency_axis_position: Openness: open (permissionless minting on fxhash, open-source generative art ethos). Commons vs. capture: tension between commons (open generative art culture, Tezos roots) and capture (VC-backed, token-incentivized). Spectacle vs. infrastructure: infrastructure (tools for generative art creation, distribution, economics). Individual vs. collective: individual artists create, but collector co-creation (fx(params), open-form) introduces collective dynamics.

infrastructure_governance.openness: Generative art code is on-chain/IPFS (open, verifiable). Platform is proprietary. $FXH token may introduce governance. Smart contracts are open. The Tezos-era ethos was strongly open-source; the move to Ethereum/Base and VC funding has introduced more proprietary elements.
infrastructure_governance.governance_model: Founding-team governance currently. $FXH token introduces potential token-holder governance but governance mechanisms not fully detailed. VC investors (1kx, USV, Coinbase Ventures) have influence through funding relationship. Community governance through curation (upvotes, collections) but not formal DAO structure.
infrastructure_governance.data_sovereignty: Art code stored on-chain or IPFS — artists retain access to their code. NFT metadata on-chain. Art coin and trading data on-chain (Base). Artists can theoretically deploy their code elsewhere. However, the platform's discovery and community features are proprietary — artist reputation and collector relationships are not portable.
infrastructure_governance.interoperability: Multichain (Tezos, Ethereum, Base). Art coins are standard ERC-20 on Base. NFTs are ERC-721. Composable with DeFi protocols. Bonding curve mechanics are standard AMM patterns. High interoperability by design. Could integrate with any EVM-compatible infrastructure.
infrastructure_governance.preservation_strategy: On-chain code storage for many projects. IPFS for metadata. Hash-deterministic rendering means the art can be reproduced from on-chain data alone if rendering environment is preserved. This is one of the strongest preservation models in digital art — but depends on JavaScript runtime availability and browser compatibility over time.
infrastructure_governance.consent_architecture: Opt-in for artists (publish work on platform). Collectors opt-in by purchasing. Art coins create secondary market that artists initiate but cannot fully control. No machine-readable consent framework for downstream use. The open-form model gives collectors creative agency within artist-defined parameters — a nuanced consent model for co-creation.

field_position.relation_to_traditional_art_world: Parallel with growing integration. Generative art from fxhash has entered traditional galleries (Bright Moments, Tender, generative art exhibitions). Art Basel events feature fxhash artists. But the core community and market remain crypto-native. The art coin model has no traditional art world equivalent.
field_position.what_it_enables: Continuous artist revenue through trading fees (not just one-time sales). Collector co-creation through fx(params) and open-form minting. On-chain, hash-deterministic generative art that is independently reproducible. Artist-specific micro-economies (art coins). Permissionless publishing of generative art without curatorial gatekeeping.
field_position.what_it_lacks: Curation at scale (the permissionless model means quality variance is extreme). Art historical context and critical discourse within the platform. Stability — the token and art coin layer introduces financial volatility that can overwhelm artistic considerations. Onboarding for non-crypto-native audiences. Clear separation between artistic and speculative activity.
field_position.who_is_excluded: Non-code-literate artists (generative art requires programming). Non-crypto-native collectors (requires wallet, ETH/tez, understanding of bonding curves). Artists working in non-generative media. Collectors without risk tolerance for volatile art coins. Users in jurisdictions with crypto restrictions. The technical and financial complexity creates significant barriers.
field_position.frontier_signal: Frontier. Art coins and bonding curves are a genuinely new economic model for artist-collector relationships. Open-form generative art is a new category. The question is whether these innovations create lasting structural change or are absorbed into speculative cycle mechanics.

attention_intention.discovery_mechanism: Platform-internal rankings, trending collections, curated highlights. Crypto Twitter/X for community discovery. Generative art community events (live mints, exhibitions). Art coin price movements generate attention. Coinbase listing provides visibility.
attention_intention.attention_dependency: High for the token/art coin layer (depends on crypto market sentiment and social media hype). Moderate for the generative art practice layer (dedicated community that persists through market cycles). The platform survived the 2022-2023 crash with reduced but stable activity, suggesting some attention-independence for the core practice.
attention_intention.intention_alignment: Mixed. The generative art marketplace infrastructure is intention-native (serves structural needs of code-based art). The art coin and bonding curve layer introduces attention-capture dynamics. The fx(params) co-creation model is strongly intention-aligned (deep creative engagement). The $FXH token airdrop and trading mechanics are attention-native.
attention_intention.commons_contribution: Significant. On-chain generative art code is a public commons contribution. The generative art vocabulary and practice norms developed on fxhash benefit the entire field. Open-form art as a concept contributes to shared creative vocabulary. However, the art coin economic model is proprietary to fxhash's infrastructure.

provenance_temporality.provenance_type: Both ownership and creative provenance. On-chain hash records the exact parameters that generated each work. Art coin history records collector economic participation. fx(params) records collector creative input as on-chain data. This is unusually rich provenance for digital art.
provenance_temporality.temporal_logic: Generative — each work is created at a specific moment with a specific hash. Open-form works have ongoing temporality (new editions can be minted over time). Art coin prices create a financial temporal layer. The platform itself has a historical arc (Tezos era → multichain → art coins).
provenance_temporality.absence_handling: Does not explicitly address field absences. Focuses on enabling new forms of creation and exchange. The permissionless model means some absences self-correct (any artist can publish) but others persist (non-code-literate artists remain excluded).

coherence.coherence_vs_consensus: Coherence. Multiple valid readings of generative art coexist on the platform — some collectors value aesthetic quality, others value rarity/hash traits, others value artist reputation, others trade art coins speculatively. The platform supports these different value frameworks simultaneously without forcing consensus.
coherence.contestability: Moderate. On-chain data is transparent and verifiable. Art coin prices are market-determined (contestable through trading). Platform-level decisions (featuring, curation) are not formally contestable. Code is open for inspection — artistic claims can be verified.
coherence.forkability: High. On-chain code and deterministic rendering mean works can theoretically be reproduced outside fxhash. Smart contract code is verifiable. Art coins follow standard ERC-20 patterns. The community and discovery layer is the main barrier to forking. Art Blocks and other platforms demonstrate that the generative art marketplace model is replicable.

adai_comparison.what_adai_should_adopt: The art coin model as a reference for how economic and creative layers can be structurally integrated. The fx(params) co-creation approach as a model for participant agency within artist-defined parameters. On-chain hash determinism as a preservation and provenance model. The principle of continuous artist revenue through trading fees rather than one-time sales. The open-form concept where collectors are co-creators rather than passive buyers.
adai_comparison.what_adai_should_refuse: The bonding curve graduation mechanics that incentivize speculation over artistic engagement. The VC-backed growth logic that pressures platform toward financialization. The permissionless model without curation — A(DAI) needs coherence, which requires editorial judgment. The token price volatility that can overwhelm artistic considerations. The complexity barriers that exclude non-technical participants.
adai_comparison.structural_tension: fxhash demonstrates that economic innovation (art coins, bonding curves) can create new creative possibilities (open-form art, co-creation) but also introduces speculative dynamics that threaten artistic integrity. A(DAI) must find the point where economic innovation serves creative practice without financializing it. The tension between fxhash's permissionless openness and A(DAI)'s need for coherence/curation is productive — A(DAI) must enable participation without drowning in noise.

regulatory_legal.regulatory_exposure: Significant. $FXH token may face securities classification (Howey test). Art coins as ERC-20 tokens could be classified as securities or financial instruments. Bonding curves are unregulated AMM mechanisms. EU MiCA regulation applies. French PSAN (digital asset service provider) licensing may apply. Coinbase listing suggests some regulatory compliance work completed. The 2024-2025 regulatory environment for token launches is more scrutinized than 2021.
regulatory_legal.ip_model: Artists retain copyright to their generative art code. On-chain code is publicly visible but copyrighted. Art coins do not transfer IP rights. NFT ownership transfers the specific output but not the underlying code. Creative Commons licensing for some projects, all-rights-reserved for others — determined by individual artists.
regulatory_legal.opt_in_vs_opt_out: Opt-in for artists (publish and optionally create art coins). Opt-in for collectors (purchase, mint, trade). Art coin trading is permissionless once created — artists cannot opt out of secondary trading on their coins. The open-form model means artist consent is given at the system design level but individual collector actions are autonomous within those parameters.

ecosystem.platform_dependency: Depends on Base L2 (Coinbase), Ethereum, and formerly Tezos. IPFS for storage. JavaScript runtime for rendering. Coinbase for $FXH listing. Multiple blockchain dependencies but the multichain approach reduces single-point-of-failure risk. Strong dependency on Coinbase ecosystem (Base + exchange listing).
ecosystem.network_effects: Moderate. Generative art community network effects (artists attract collectors, collectors attract artists). Art coin liquidity creates trading network effects. But the community is relatively small compared to larger NFT platforms. Cross-pollination with Art Blocks and wider generative art community provides network benefits.
ecosystem.post_crash_trajectory: Survived and evolved. Migrated from Tezos-only to multichain. Launched $FXH token and art coins on Base (2025). Community remained active through the crash at reduced scale. The pivot to art coins and token economics is a growth strategy beyond the post-crash NFT marketplace model. Current trajectory is experimental growth from a resilient but small base.
